# SpreadBounds — how unevenly survivors can spread

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: new, not yet proved

Any two equal intervals of the cycle hold survivor counts differing by at most two to the number of wheels. With wheels 2 and 3 frozen, the two columns' survivor counts up to any point differ by at most two to the number of remaining wheels.

## Planned

**Will rest on:** no other node

**Planned claims:** `interval_spread_bound`, `column_imbalance_bound`

**Evidence so far:** Both checked numerically (4,761 cases). The column imbalance reaches 18 at the wheels up to 23, against a bound of 128.

**Scope:** Tier 1: inclusion-exclusion.

- Source: [D. H. Lehmer, The distribution of totatives, Canad. J. Math. 7 (1955), 347-357](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/A1B6054448396406512E4ECE51DC6ADD/S0008414X00030467a.pdf/distribution_of_totatives.pdf) — Theorems 9 and 10, the interval form
